articles.title: That Giggle? It's a 15-Million-Year-Old Echo of How We Learned to Talk
articles.summary: A new study reveals that the rhythmic pattern in human laughter is shared by all great apes and has remained unchanged since our last common ancestor 15 million years ago. This finding offers a rare glimpse into the evolution of speech.

articles.title: A Whisper from the Dawn of Time: Could a Tiny Black Hole Solve the Dark Matter Mystery?
articles.summary: A gravitational wave signal detected by LIGO may come from a primordial black hole—an object formed just after the Big Bang. If confirmed, it could explain dark matter, the invisible substance making up 85% of the universe's mass.

articles.title: Cosmic Cotton Candy: Astronomers Find Two Planets Lighter Than Fairy Floss
articles.summary: Two newly confirmed exoplanets, TOI-791 b and c, are Jupiter-sized but have densities lower than cotton candy. Discovered with help from citizen scientists, they orbit in a rare resonance and offer clues about planetary formation.
